summary: artifact_produced_outbox.emitter admits 'object_snapshot_mint' (cinatra#3028, epic #3023, lifecycle-c W4 — enabler 0.13, the object-backed contract) — the operator-upgrade twin of the fresh-install bootstrap leaf artifactReviewGateSchemaQueries in src/lib/artifacts/artifact-review-gate-schema.ts, widened in the SAME PR. WHY: the plan's section 3 fixes the object-backed contract — an object-backed type's display receives a discriminated projection, the live object data or a minted snapshot revision, and minting the snapshot is what makes a row reviewable, so the produced event is emitted AT THE MINT and never at the raw row write. The mint is therefore a new produced-event choke point, and the produced-event contract enumerates its emitters as a CLOSED set because that set is the audit surface the orchestration wiring and the reconciliation sweeper reason over; the mint is not the CMS staged write and must not borrow its emitter, or 'which road produced this' becomes unanswerable. THE DEFECT THIS CLOSES: the emitter column carries an inline CHECK created with the table, admitting exactly the three emitters that existed then, so on an upgraded instance the mint's INSERT raises inside the capture's own transaction and the WHOLE snapshot capture rolls back — an object-backed row would be un-snapshottable and therefore unreviewable, with the failure surfacing as a constraint violation nowhere near the contract that caused it. SHAPE: idempotent DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS + ADD CONSTRAINT — postgres names a column CHECK <table>_<column>_check deterministically — so this is a no-op on a schema the bootstrap already created wide and a widen on every deployed one; the exact idiom core__0097 used on artifact_review_audit. STRICTLY ADDITIVE in effect: every value the old constraint admitted is still admitted, so no committed outbox row can become invalid, no row is rewritten, and the re-validation scan the ADD CONSTRAINT performs passes by construction. Recorded as destructive because the convention's classifier enumerates ADD CONSTRAINT over existing rows as such, and that classification is not argued with here. DOWN narrows the CHECK back to the three-emitter vocabulary and FAILS on an instance that has already minted an object-backed snapshot — the correct failure, because deleting an outbox row to make a revert succeed would drop a review the product opened. Unqualified names ride the runner's search_path (the app schema). SEQ 0099 — 0098 is claimed on another branch of this epic; 0099 is the next free sequence at authoring time. migrations/** is HIGH-RISK: owner approval required; the lane never merges.
